newsitem.title: USA: Contempt threat for two ex-administration aides.
newsitem.headline: Contempt threat for two ex-administration aides.

text.p: The chairman of a House committee investigating campaign fundraising said Friday he would seek contempt charges against two former administration officials if they refused to turn over subpoenaed documents.

Webster Hubbell, a former associate attorney general, and former Commerce Department official John Huang wrote the House Government Reform Committee Thursday that they were invoking their constitutional right against possible self-incrimination and would not comply with committee subpoenas.

"We're moving forward to compel a full and complete repsonse to the committee's subpoenas for documents from Mr. Huang and Mr. Hubbell. We are pursuing all legal channels in our attempt to obtain these subpoenaed records," Chairman Dan Burton, an Indiana Republican, said in a statement.

Burton said if Huang and Hubbell continued to defy the subpoenas, he would schedule a committee vote to find them in contempt of Congress, which could send both men to jail if they were found guilty in court.
Hubbell was a long time friend of President Clinton and was a law partner of Hillary Rodham Clinton at the Rose law firm in Little Rock, Arkansas, before Clinton was elected.

Huang raised funds for the Democratic party from Asian-Americans after he left the Commerce Department. Almost half of the $3.4 million he brought in has since been returned by the party because of questions about its sources.
